name: Syntropic sandy hillside · above the zen garden
notes:
Top of the old W3 lobe, between the hairpin, the driveway and the road edge: sandier topsoil, so this is where syntropy starts and builds uphill over time.
Planting: dragon fruit climbing posts and pioneer trunks; early pioneers (pigeon pea, cassava, papaya, banana) for fast cover and chop-and-drop; pineapple in rows on contour to hold the soil; other quick perennials in the gaps.
Then: as the pioneers are cut back, fruit trees go in, and the system creeps up the hill into W3 row by row.
Water: rain-fed, with half-moon basins and chop-and-drop pushed onto the contour. Keep it low and green on the road edge (fire).
